title: Notification
description: One out-of-band notice to the operator (the notify plugin, docs/design/notifications.md): what happened, which request, run, pool, or account it is about, and the exact commands to act, made from one recorded event only. 1.1 adds the kind `review.expiring`. 1.2 adds the kind `dispatch.started`. The body of the webhook's POST, and the text of a desktop notification. It names ids, classes, kinds, and times; it never carries a secret, a prompt, an answer, a request's summary, or a command a request would run.

id.description: `<kind>:<subject>:<event seq>`: the same event never makes two notices of one kind.

kind.description: approval.opened: a request was queued; approval.expiring: an open request expires within the configured lead time (unanswered, it is denied); run.user-action: a step or run failed with disposition USER_ACTION; run.escalated: a step was escalated to a higher tier after its result was rejected; run.waiting: a step waits for an assigned account's limit to reset (ADR-0052 wait); pool.limited: a resource pool closed at its limit; worker.quarantined: an agent account was quarantined, so its Workers take no work (PROP-0012 E); review.expiring (1.1): a board task's review held for the operator expires within the configured lead time (unanswered, the task waits for input, review-expired); dispatch.started (1.2): System started a ready board task's run by itself where the project's policy gives dispatch notify (PROP-0014 D2).

subject.description: What the notice is about, and what deduplication counts by: the request id, the workflow run id, the pool id, the agent account id (`<provider>:slot-<n>` for a slot with no account id yet), or the board task id.

at.description: When the event was recorded; for approval.expiring and review.expiring, when the reminder was made.

event.description: The event-log entry the notice was made from.

text.description: What happened and what is at stake, in one or two sentences.

act.description: The exact commands the operator runs to act, most direct first.

link.description: The operator page (`/ui`) without its token: it opens where the page already holds one; `system ui` prints the link with the token.
